findings.evidence: `def CompletelyMonotoneOn` at line 88 has no `@[expose]` (contrast `@[expose] def IsCompletelyMonotone` line 176, `@[expose] def IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi` line 328); the file's own proofs need `rw [CompletelyMonotoneOn]` (lines 140, 157, 165, 199), which is only possible inside this module. The same pattern is already handled correctly for the unexposed `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIci` by `isCompletelyMonotoneOnIci_iff ... := Iff.rfl` (lines 432, 437).
findings.fix: Add the definitional restatement, e.g. `theorem completelyMonotoneOn_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg {f : ℝ → ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} : CompletelyMonotoneOn f s ↔ AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (fun u => f (-u)) (-s) := (Iff.rfl)` (parenthesized `rfl` so consumers do not depend on defeq), and use it in place of the in-module `rw [CompletelyMonotoneOn]` at lines 140, 157, 165, 199. Keep the body unexposed.
findings.issue: `CompletelyMonotoneOn` is a `def` without `@[expose]`, and no lemma restates it as `AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (fun u => f (-u)) (-s)`. The only exported characterization is `iff_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg`, which assumes `UniqueDiffOn ℝ s` — exactly the hypothesis the Taylor-witness formulation exists to avoid. A consumer therefore cannot introduce or eliminate `CompletelyMonotoneOn f s` on a non-uniquely-differentiable `s` unless `f` is globally `ContDiff` (`of_contDiff`), nor transfer any other `AbsolutelyMonotoneOn` result to it.

findings.evidence: grep for `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg` across `code/` returns only its own declaration (line 197); the former users `IsCompletelyMonotone.add`/`.smul` were rewritten to use `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_completelyMonotoneOn` (lines 274, 280). Its proof (lines 199-203) is just the new bridge plus `-(Ici 0) = Iic 0` (`Set.neg_Ici`, used at Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/Integral.lean:86).
findings.fix: Delete `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg`; `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_completelyMonotoneOn` together with the general `_def` lemma requested above supplies it in one `rw` chain.
findings.issue: `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg` is now duplicated API: it is the composite of `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_completelyMonotoneOn` (line 189) with the definitional unfolding plus `Set.neg_Ici`, and after this PR it has no caller in the repository, leaving two `Iff` bridges for the same fact.

findings.fix: Annotate `CompletelyMonotoneOn.contDiffOn` with `@[grind →]` and `CompletelyMonotoneOn.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg` with `@[grind =>]`, matching the in-file convention.
findings.issue: The new eliminators `CompletelyMonotoneOn.contDiffOn` (line 100) and `CompletelyMonotoneOn.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg` (line 121) carry no `@[grind]` annotation, while every structurally identical eliminator for the sibling predicates in this file does; `grind` will discharge goals from `IsCompletelyMonotone` but not from the new general predicate.

summary: The new `CompletelyMonotoneOn` has an unexposed body and no `_def`/iff restatement, so downstream it is a sealed predicate with no usable API precisely on the non-`UniqueDiffOn` sets it was introduced to serve. Additionally the old `isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg` is now a duplicate bridge with no caller, and the new eliminators lack the `@[grind]` annotations their in-file analogues carry.
